"D'AUTRES SIGNAUX SONT NÉCESSAIRES" Zaporijjia, qui comptait plus de 700.000 habitants avant la guerre, est régulièrement visée par les bombardements russes, dont l'intensité s'est accrue au cours des derniers mois. "La nuit dernière a constitué une nouvelle confirmation que la Russie considère tout allègement de la pression comme un signal lui permettant soi-disant de continuer à faire la guerre, de continuer à larguer des bombes sur les villes. D'autres signaux sont nécessaires", a déclaré Volodimir Zelensky. Une attaque de missile menée samedi après-midi a également frappé un restaurant à Kyiv, blessant sept personnes. Des drones russes ont survolé la capitale ukrainienne tout au long de la journée dans le cadre d'une nouvelle vague massive de bombardements, la plus importante depuis les premiers jours de la guerre. Le ministère russe de la Défense a déclaré samedi en début se soirée que ses drones avaient frappé plus tôt un centre de traitement de données à Kyiv ainsi qu'un cargo transportant des fournitures militaires vers le port ukrainien d'Odessa. Dans un communiqué, il a ajouté que le site de Kyiv était utilisé par les forces armées ukrainiennes pour collecter, traiter et stocker des renseignements. Reuters n'a pas été en mesure de vérifier ces informations dans l'immédiat. La décision de Donald Trump de lever les sanctions sur les exportations de diesel russe intervient alors que son administration cherche à enrayer la hausse des prix des carburants, qui ont bondi dans le contexte du conflit opposant les États-Unis à l'Iran. Kyiv avait au contraire exhorté Washington à accroître la pression sur la Russie afin de la contraindre à engager de véritables négociations pour mettre fin à la guerre, qui dure depuis quatre ans et demi. L'ACCORD SUR LE DIESEL A PRIS KYIV PAR SURPRISE Donald Trump a en outre critiqué les frappes ukrainiennes contre les raffineries russes, estimant qu'elles avaient contribué à faire grimper les prix mondiaux. Kyiv dit vouloir un arrêt total des attaques visant les infrastructures énergétiques des deux camps, alors que Moscou continue de pilonner le réseau électrique ukrainien. Samedi, plusieurs secteurs de Kyiv et de sa région ont été privés d'électricité, provoquant l'arrêt complet du métro de la capitale pour la deuxième fois de la semaine. Ces dernières frappes sont intervenues après des discussions à Miami entre responsables ukrainiens et européens et négociateurs américains, vendredi, en vue d'élaborer une proposition commune pour mettre fin à la guerre, selon une source proche du dossier. L'agence de presse officielle russe Tass, citant une source, a rapporté samedi que les émissaires américains Steve Witkoff et Jared Kushner pourraient se rendre à Moscou au cours des deux prochaines semaines. Donald Trump a annoncé l'accord sur le diesel alors que les négociations de vendredi étaient en cours, une décision qui, selon Volodimir Zelensky, a pris Kyiv par surprise. Le président russe Vladimir Poutine a déclaré, à l'issue d'un entretien téléphonique avec son homologue américain, qu'une reprise immédiate des pourparlers de paix était peu probable, invoquant les attaques de drones ukrainiens contre Moscou. Par ailleurs, quatre civils ont été tués et cinq autres blessés à la suite d'attaques ukrainiennes contre la région de Louhansk, sous contrôle russe dans l'est de l'Ukraine, a déclaré samedi le gouverneur local installé par Moscou. Reuters n'a pas été en mesure de vérifier cette information de manière indépendante et l'Ukraine n'a pas fait de commentaire dans l'immédiat.

item.title: Norris apologises after collision dashes McLaren sprint hopes
item.description: World champion Lando Norris apologised to his McLaren team after a final-lap collision with team mate Oscar Piastri wrecked their pursuit of a podium finish at a chaotic Singapore Grand Prix sprint on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Rohith Nair
item.content:encoded: World champion Lando Norris apologised to his McLaren team after a final-lap collision with team mate Oscar Piastri wrecked their pursuit of a podium finish at a [USN:L1N45W02M TEXT:"chaotic Singapore Grand Prix sprint"] on Saturday. The McLaren duo were chasing Ferrari's Charles Leclerc, who was struggling with his tyres in the dying stages of the 20-lap sprint, when disaster struck on the final lap. Norris, running fifth behind Piastri in fourth, attempted to overtake his team mate but clipped the Australian's rear tyre with his front wheel, sending both cars spinning and handing Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli fourth place. "Sorry about that. Obviously I didn't want that to happen but I thought I was fully alongside. I just ran out of space at the apex but I was there," Norris said over the team radio. While Norris limped home to eighth place to claim the final point available, Piastri was forced to retire as he became one of nine cars that did not finish - a record number of retirements for a Formula One sprint race. "I'd rather just go back and review it," Norris told Sky Sports. "I apologised to them that one of the cars is out but, like I said, the rest of it we'll go review." Piastri said he had not seen the incident properly to comment but downplayed its significance as they were not in high points scoring positions. "From where I sit, it's for fourth and fifth for a sprint race, so I'm not that bothered either way," Piastri said. "Just obviously it's a lot of work now for the team to get both cars fixed (ahead of qualifying for Sunday's race). Just a shame for the team." 'SIMPLY NOT ACCEPTABLE' Both McLaren drivers were summoned to meet the stewards after the collision but no further action was taken. The FIA said both drivers "contributed to the incident and that neither driver was wholly or predominantly to blame for the collision." McLaren team principal Andrea Stella was not impressed with his drivers, however, adding that scoring just one point was not enough. "Seeing two McLarens making contact like that is simply not acceptable. This is something that we will discuss with our drivers," he said. "We will do it in private. We will reiterate that the team interest is far bigger than any of us. There's no ego, there's no person that is bigger than the interest of the McLaren Formula One team. "I'm sure, like always, this will be conversations that will lead to the team being more united and even stronger." Red Bull's Max Verstappen won the sprint and the Dutchman, who also [USN:L1N45W02M TEXT:"clinched pole for Sunday's race"] , leapfrogged Norris to climb to fifth in the world championship standings.

item.title: EU's Irish presidency wants 8% cut to proposed 2028-2034 budget plan
item.description: The Irish EU presidency proposed on Saturday an 8% cut in the European Commission's budget plan for the period 2028 to 2034 to €1.6 trillion ($1.79 trillion), drawing criticism from more frugal member states that the reduction is not deep enough.
item.dc:creator: Jan Strupczewski, Yun Chee Foo
item.content:encoded: The Irish EU presidency proposed on Saturday an 8% cut in the European Commission's budget plan for the period 2028 to 2034 to €1.6 trillion ($1.79 trillion), drawing criticism from more frugal member states that the reduction is not deep enough. The Irish proposal still marks a 30% increase over the bloc's current budget, which runs from 2021 to 2027. The EU budget is the main source of financing for all of the 27-country bloc's main policies. The Commission, the EU executive, has said the bloc needs to spend more on defence and boosting European competitiveness, while some member states want to retain most of the expenditure to support farming and regional development. "The Negotiating Box provides savings of 8%, or €141 billion, on the Commission's original proposal," said Ireland, current holder of the EU's six-month rotating presidency, referring to its compromise proposal. Ireland put the Commission's original €2 trillion figure adjusted for inflation over the seven-year period at €1.76 trillion based on 2025 prices, which resulted in an 8% reduction. IRELAND SAYS PLAN SEEKS TO RECONCILE COMPETING DEMANDS "As we see it, the negotiating box acts to bridge the many differences between the member states," Irish minister Thomas Byrne told a press conference. "It brings us closer to resolving the budgetary trilemma, addressing the talks of how best to finance new priorities in competitiveness, research, innovation, security and defence while at the same time addressing core policies," he said. The proposal sets out a 3% cut in spending on regional development, agriculture and fisheries from the Commission's own figures — the biggest outlay in the budget — and a 13% reduction in spending on competitiveness and security. It foresees €55 billion in new financing options derived from customs duties, a share of the cash EU governments get from selling CO2 emissions permits to companies and an annual lump-sum contribution from large companies operating in the EU, among other sources. Germany's Chancellor Friedrich Merz joined ministers from Sweden and the Netherlands - all three countries are net contributors to the budget - in criticising the Irish proposal. "The EU budget must be affordable for those who bear the main burden of financing it," he said. However, lawmakers in the European Parliament, which wants a 10% increase in the Commission's €2 trillion proposal, said the Irish plan would weaken Europe and would not win their consent. EU leaders will discuss the Irish proposal in Brussels on October 15 to 16. The EU budget, which is known as the [USN:L8N41B114 TEXT:"Multiannual Financial Framework"], needs to be agreed by all 27 member states. ($1 = 0.8928 euros)

item.title: Israeli strikes kill five people in Gaza, medics say
item.description: Israeli strikes killed at least five Palestinians in the Gaza Strip in two separate attacks on Saturday, health officials said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Israeli strikes killed at least five Palestinians in the Gaza Strip in two separate attacks on Saturday, health officials said. Medics said an Israeli strike killed four people near Panda Mall in Gaza City, while another killed one person in the Tuffah neighbourhood further south of the city. The Israeli military said the two strikes targeted militants, without giving further information. Israel has stepped up strikes against Hamas in recent weeks, saying the Palestinian militant group has been rearming and carrying out attacks in violation of the ceasefire. Hamas denies rebuilding its arsenal or planning attacks and accuses Israel of undermining a US-brokered ceasefire agreed a year ago. The ceasefire calls for eventual reconstruction of the territory. But little progress has been made towards implementing a deal to end the conflict that includes terms for Hamas to disarm and Israel to withdraw its troops. Gaza health officials have said at least 1,400 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli fire since the truce was agreed last October. Israel says four of its soldiers have been killed by militants in Gaza over the same period. The Gaza war was triggered by the Hamas-led [USN:L1N45T04T TEXT:"October 7, 2023 attacks"] on Israel, which killed 1,200 people, while a further 251 were taken hostage. Israel's subsequent bombardment and ground operations in Gaza have killed more than 74,000 people, according to Gaza health officials.

item.title: Palmer signs Chelsea contract until 2034
item.description: The England international has become a key figure since joining Chelsea from Manchester City.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Chelsea attacking midfielder Cole Palmer has signed a contract extension to keep him at Stamford Bridge until 2034, the Premier League club said on Saturday. The 24-year-old England international has become a key figure since joining Chelsea from Manchester City in 2023, scoring 91 goals in 138 appearances across all competitions. He was part of the squad that won the Club World Cup and UEFA Conference League. "Speaking to the owners, to the sporting directors and obviously the manager, they gave me a lot of confidence so it was only right to sign," Palmer said. "Speaking to players as well, everyone has the same ambitions. I feel like we win major trophies here consistently." Chelsea have agreed long-term contracts Chelsea with several first-team players and emerging talent. Forward [USN:L6N44J020 TEXT:"Joao Pedro"] recently signed a deal through 2034, and winger Pedro Neto agreed a six-year contract last month. Chelsea, 10th in the Premier League table, host Bournemouth on Saturday.

item.title: Verstappen claims first Singapore win as nine retirements mar chaotic sprint
item.description: The victory was the first of any kind for the Dutchman in Singapore as he took the chequered flag ahead of Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc.
item.dc:creator: Rohith Nair
item.content:encoded: Red Bull's Max Verstappen tasted victory in Singapore for the first time as the polesitter won a chaotic sprint on Saturday after the [USN:L1N45W02H TEXT:"start was delayed by over 30 minutes"] due to heavy rain while nine cars retired, a record for sprint races. The victory was the first of any kind for the Dutchman in Singapore as he took the chequered flag ahead of Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc. "I want to win tomorrow. I don't see this as a win in terms of actually winning a Grand Prix," Verstappen said. Mercedes' championship leader Kimi Antonelli was gifted fourth place after the two McLarens collided on the final lap while his team mate George Russell crashed out of the lead on lap one. Verstappen had kept his [USN:L1N45V0HG TEXT:"pole position"] after escaping a penalty for overtaking under a yellow flag on Friday but the Dutchman made a slow start as Russell stormed ahead and Hamilton swiftly moved up from sixth to third. Russell's sprint ended on the last turn of lap one when his rear tyre went over the kerb and he spun into the wall to bring the safety car out. "The start was horrendous again, so that's definitely something that we need to improve on because if you have something like that tomorrow, that's your race over if nothing crazy happens," Verstappen added. "After that, you just want to keep it calm and under control because you know that you can't pass around here." 'SILLY MISTAKE' FOR RUSSELL Russell said a miscalculation caused him to spin out at the last corner. "I came through the corner, had more battery deployment than I thought. Pushed me a little bit wider than I hoped and then I just went on the white line," Russell said. "Yeah, silly mistake. Big, big consequences." The carnage continued when Lance Stroll and Sergio Perez retired after they collided and Red Bull's Isack Hadjar was asked to stop his car due to a technical issue. The safety car remained on track after Franco Colapinto's Alpine also came to a standstill and they did not resume racing until lap seven. Verstappen led from the Ferraris of Hamilton and Leclerc while the McLarens of Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris were in the top five ahead of Antonelli. MCLARENS COLLIDE ON FINAL LAP McLaren's hopes of a podium vanished, however, when reigning champion Norris nudged into Piastri and the two cars spun out, allowing Antonelli to move up to fourth place and stretch his championship lead over Russell to 89 points. "I checked in my mirrors and I saw red lights of the back of the cars of the McLarens. So I knew that something happened," Leclerc said. The qualifying session for Sunday's race was delayed due to the rain.

item.title: Amelia Earhart expedition heads to Pacific atoll hoping to find her plane
item.description: A US-based team of marine archaeologists has set sail for a tiny island in the far western Pacific seeking to examine the latest tantalizing clue to one of the 20th century's great unsolved mysteries: the 1937 disappearance of famed aviator Amelia Earhart.
item.dc:creator: Steve Gorman
item.content:encoded: A US-based team of marine archaeologists has set sail for a tiny island in the far western Pacific seeking to examine the latest tantalizing clue to one of the 20th century's great unsolved mysteries: the 1937 disappearance of famed aviator Amelia Earhart. Backed by Purdue University, an institution long affiliated with Earhart and her legacy, the group aims to learn whether a submerged object detected by satellite imagery in the island's lagoon six years ago is the wreckage of Earhart's twin-engine Lockheed Electra 10-E airplane. Such a finding would conclusively prove the hypothesis of some scholars that Earhart and her navigator, Fred Noonan, crash-landed on or near the coral-ringed atoll and perished as castaways there, hundreds of miles from their intended refueling stop. After embarking from Los Angeles earlier this month, the group was expected to arrive on Tuesday, October 13, local time at Nikumaroro, an uninhabited speck of land in the remote Phoenix Islands, part of the archipelago nation of the Kiribati Republic. "Finding Amelia Earhart's Electra aircraft would be the discovery of a lifetime," Richard Pettigrew, head of the Archaeological Legacy Institute in Eugene, Oregon, who is leading the effort in conjunction with Purdue, said in press materials for the mission. Purdue general counsel and expedition member Steve Schultz, who was in Fiji conducting advance work for the expedition last week, said in an interview: "This would be solving one of the great mysteries in aviation history, certainly one of the great mysteries of the 20th century," The mission has its skeptics. Chief among them is rival Earhart explorer Ric Gillespie, co-founder of TIGHAR, short for The International Group for Historic Aircraft Recovery, and author of the 2024 "One More Good Flight: The Amelia Earhart Tragedy." TREE OR PLANE? Gillespie has led a dozen expeditions of his own to the atoll over three decades and is the leading proponent of the Nikumaroro castaway theory. But he predicted the Pettigrew-Purdue team would find no airplane wreckage or anything else of consequence left on the island. The Purdue team credits Gillespie for laying the foundation of the theory they hope to prove. And they cite a compelling body of evidence that he has amassed over the years, including human artifacts recovered on the island, such as a 1930s-era glass cosmetic jar for freckle cream and remnants of a jackknife like one Earhart carried on the plane. Gillespie's investigation also encompassed modern forensic analysis from records of measurements of skeletal remains found on the island in the 1940s; logs of radio transmission bearings from distress calls picked up by wireless operators in the days immediately after Earhart vanished; and a photograph taken of the island's shoreline months later showing an object that Gillespie said appears to be the Electra's landing gear. In a Reuters interview last week, Gillespie said he believes the plane has since been lost to history, eventually swept by tides off the coral flat where it had landed largely intact and carried into the sea to sink and break apart in the surf. Two previous attempts to locate the plane's wreckage in the surrounding ocean, including a 2019 operation conducted by marine archaeologist Robert Ballard, famed for his discovery of the wreck of the Titanic, proved fruitless, Gillespie said. A plane-shaped sonar image from elsewhere on the sea floor turned out to be a pile of rocks. "I'd love to find that airplane. It ain't gonna happen," Gillespie said. Pettigrew and his team are betting otherwise. To them, the multi-branched shape first noticed in a 2020 satellite image resembles an aircraft fuselage and wings. They assert that the object, or part of it, has since been spotted in earlier aerial images of the island's lagoon dating as far back as 1938. Gillespie said he is certain that the object in question was actually a fallen pandanus tree, a palm-like evergreen native to the island region, that washed into the lagoon. "You can see the root ball. You can see the branches," Gillespie said in the interview. "It's a tree. People see what they want to see." 'GAS IS RUNNING LOW' The official US government view has long been that the Electra ran out of fuel and crashed at sea near its refueling destination of Howland Island, another dot of land about 400 miles northwest of Nikumaroro, then known as Gardner Island. Earhart was last seen taking off in her Electra on July 2, 1937, from Papua New Guinea en route to Gardner, about 2,500 miles (4,000 km) to the east, during a multi-stage attempt to become the first woman to pilot a plane around the world. Definitive radio contact with the plane was lost the next day after Earhart, 39, reported "gas is running low," followed by her final known transmission giving her geographical line of position. The disappearance spawned the largest US government search ever undertaken for a lost aircraft, including a flyover of Gardner, but no trace of the Electra or its crew was found at the time. The $900,000 Purdue mission, consisting of 17 people, plans to remain on Nikumaroro for five days before making the six-day return boat trip to the Kiribati capital, Tarawa, according to Schultz. Purdue, based in West Lafayette, Indiana, would ultimately seek to bring back any bits of the Lockheed Electra that might be recovered. Earhart was essentially a visiting faculty member at Purdue for two years as a women's career counselor and advisor to the school's aeronautics department. A Purdue research grant paid for development of the Electra, which she called her "flying laboratory." Purdue lawyer Schultz said if the plane were found, no artifacts would be removed from it on this trip. Any effort to extract the aircraft wreckage would require further permission from the Kiribati government, he said.

item.title: 「台湾は中国の一部」、中国が台湾総統の演説非難
item.description: ［北京 １０日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［北京　１０日　ロイター］ - 中国国務院台湾事務弁公室は１０日、台湾の頼清徳総統が同日行った双十節（建国記念日）の演説について、「事実を無視し、真実をゆがめ、民衆を惑わし、下心をあらわにしている」と非難した。

同弁公室は、頼氏が演説で「『台湾独立』の分裂主義思想にかたくなに固執」し、「中国本土の脅威」を誇張したと指摘した。その上で「世界に中国は一つしかなく、台湾は中国の一部だ。これこそが台湾海峡の真の現状だ」と主張した。

台湾の将来についても「台湾同胞を含む全ての中国人民が共同で決定することができ、またそうでなければならない」と述べた。

頼清徳総統は演説で、台湾は平和を大切にするが自由を放棄することはないと述べ、台湾の人々が生存する権利は尊重されなければならないと訴えた。

item.title: Hastings like a local
item.description: Our desk editor’s guide to castle views, shipwrecks and seasonal festivals.
item.dc:creator: Alexandra Hudson
item.content:encoded: REUTERS/Illustration/Kate Evans Famous for the eponymous battle of 1066 that inspired the Bayeux Tapestry , the British seaside town of Hastings — my home of the last decade — has a thriving cultural life, magnificent natural setting and rough-around-the-edges charm that grows on you quickly. The beach is the star attraction, atmospheric pubs and cafes abound, and of course there are Hastings' evocative historical sites — not least the ruined Hastings Castle , constructed by William, Duke of Normandy, after winning the English throne. I grew up in Brighton, also on the country's southern coast, and settled in Hastings with my family after postings in Berlin, Amsterdam, and Istanbul for Reuters. The sea air and screeching seagulls made it quickly feel like home. Hastings is not immune to the problems affecting Britain's coastal towns, including a lack of employment and some deprivation, and it has seen its fortunes rise and fall over the decades. But the town is drawing more visitors and blossoming with fresh energy and new ventures. Here is how to visit Hastings like a local: Getting around: Hastings and neighbouring St Leonards-on-Sea, once a Regency-era resort and now the edgier of the two, form one urban area that is best explored on foot. Walking from central St Leonards to Hastings along the seafront promenade takes less than one hour. The elegant apartment blocks give way to British seaside staples like mini golf, go-karts and amusement arcades before you reach the Old Town, with its compact streets of timbered houses. People relax at Goat Ledge beach cafe at St Leonards-on-Sea, next to Hastings, Britain, October 4, 2026. REUTERS/Toby Melville People relax at a cafe on West Hill in Hastings Old Town, Hastings, Britain, October 4, 2026. REUTERS/Toby Melville A person views Hastings Old Town and Hastings beach as they travel on the funicular railway on East Hill. REUTERS/Toby Melville A view of Battle Abbey, built on the site of the Battle of Hastings in 1066, in Battle. REUTERS/Toby Melville A view of Battle Abbey, through a tower window, which was built on the site of the Battle of Hastings in 1066, in Battle. REUTERS/Toby Melville People relax among the remains of Hastings Castle, built in 1066 by William the Conqueror. REUTERS/Toby Melville A fisherman throws equipment from a boat after returning from a fishing trip in The Stade area of Hastings Old Town. Hastings has one of the largest working beach-launched fishing fleets in Europe. REUTERS/Toby Melville A person fishes off the harbour wall in Hastings Old Town. REUTERS/Toby Melville People walk on Hastings Pier, styled on the deck of an ocean liner. REUTERS/Toby Melville Hastings Old Town, Hastings Pier and Hastings beach are viewed from East Hill. REUTERS/Toby Melville People walk past Hastings Contemporary art gallery in Hastings Old Town. REUTERS/Toby Melville A drone view shows the beach and seafront at Hastings and St Leonards-on-Sea. REUTERS/Toby Melville People walk through George Street in Hastings Old Town. REUTERS/Toby Melville A drone view shows Hastings Pier and the seafront at Hastings and St Leonards-on-Sea. REUTERS/Toby Melville People walk past houses in Hastings Old Town. REUTERS/Toby Melville A person views old fishing net huts in The Stade area of Hastings Old Town. REUTERS/Toby Melville Mummified cats, which were discovered inside the pub walls, allegedly from the seventeenth century and preserved to ward off evil spirits, are displayed inside the Stag Inn in Hastings Old Town. REUTERS/Toby Melville Signs are attached to a lamppost in Hastings Old Town. REUTERS/Toby Melville A person buys fish from a fish shop in the Stade fishing harbour area of Hastings Old Town. REUTERS/Toby Melville People relax in the sun outside a pub in Hastings Old Town. REUTERS/Toby Melville A carriage of the funicular railway on East Hill runs in Hastings Old Town. REUTERS/Toby Melville Participants attend the annual May Day bank holiday Jack In The Green parade and festival. REUTERS/Toby Melville Children carry fishing nets as they walk toward the beach in Hastings Old Town. REUTERS/Toby Melville People fish off the harbor wall at sunrise in Hastings Old Town. REUTERS/Toby Melville If arriving by train, alight at St Leonards Warrior Square station and walk down Kings Road, a vibrant street of cafes, second-hand bookshops, vintage furniture stores and artist-run outlets selling bold screenprints and ceramics. It holds a street market on the first Saturday of each month, featuring handicrafts, organic food, and jewellery. Turn left at the end of the road for your first glimpse of the sea. What to see: One of my favourite spots on the beach is the strip along Warrior Square and Bottle Alley, a split-level promenade. Beachfront cafes such as Goat Ledge , Starsky & Hatch and The Selkie have breathed new life into this area, and it is a popular place to bask in the sun with a coffee or lunch. The brightly painted wooden huts, twinkly lights and bistro tables on the pebbles bring a festival vibe and you’ll often hear live music here. A short walk further along the seafront brings you to George Street, a charming pedestrian lane of restaurants, pubs and gift shops at the foot of the castle. The West Hill lift is a historic Victorian funicular railway that will transport you up to the Norman castle for £5.50 ($7.40) round-trip. There you’ll find magnificent views across the English Channel towards France, as well as yoga classes and outdoor film screenings. The West Hill is also home to the Smugglers Adventure , a fun attraction that tells stories of piracy and smuggling in a warren of caves reputedly once used to conceal contraband. In the 1960s, the caves housed a subterranean nightclub. To return to the Old Town, hop back on the funicular or follow one of the several steep, winding paths. Look out for the twittens — narrow, medieval alleyways between the houses, as you weave through All Saints Street, Tackleway and the High Street. What to eat: If you fancy seafood, the grilled “catch of the day” fish bap (or sandwich) at Goat Ledge is always delicious. Alternatively, pick up traditional fish and chips and eat them on the beach. Just watch out for diving seagulls going for your chips. People relax at Goat Ledge beach cafe at St Leonards-on-Sea. REUTERS/Toby Melville People relax at Selkie Seafood Bar at St Leonards-on-Sea. REUTERS/Toby Melville Oyster shells and other sea food are seen on a beachside table at Selkie Seafood Bar at St Leonards-on-Sea. REUTERS/Toby Melville In St Leonards, Half Man! Half Burger! has some of the best burgers — meat and vegetarian — I've ever tasted, and Three Faces has incredible tapas. Culture fix: Hastings is unusual in having a beach-launched fishing fleet, with the boats hauled back on to the pebbles when not in use. Right beside them is Hastings Contemporary , a wonderful art gallery whose design mirrors that of the historic black Net Shops used for stowing fishing equipment. A fisherman throws equipment from a boat after returning from a fishing trip in The Stade area of Hastings Old Town. Hastings has one of the largest working beach-launched fishing fleets in Europe. REUTERS/Toby Melville A tractor pulls a fishing boat up the beach in The Stade area of Hastings Old Town. REUTERS/Toby Melville Walk along Rock-a-Nore Road and stop at the excellent (and free) Fishermen's Museum , which highlights the history of the fleet and tragic storms that have struck. Opposite is the 1902 East Hill lift, Britain's steepest funicular, which takes you up to Hastings Country Park — a beautiful expanse of rolling sandstone cliffs, with breathtaking views down to the sea. Look out for the roaming ponies that graze the heathland. A young person views exhibits at the Fishermen's Museum in Hastings Old Town. REUTERS/Toby Melville For music lovers, Hastings Philharmonic runs excellent classical concerts throughout the year. Check the tides: Hastings has a pebble beach, but at low tide, vast stretches of sand are exposed, offering ample space for long strolls. I like to time sea swims for high tide and beach walks for low tide. If this falls at sunset, you'll find the beach packed with locals savouring the views. Look out for hagstones, pebbles with natural holes. A few times a year, when the tide falls below 60 cm (2 feet), you can glimpse the wreck of the Amsterdam, a Dutch East India Company ship that ran aground in 1749 outside St Leonards and was exposed by shifting sands in 1969. It makes for an eerie sight. A replica is moored outside Amsterdam's Maritime Museum , while Hastings' excellent Shipwreck Museum displays the bottles, spoons and other goods found onboard. The 1066 battlefield: A 15-minute train ride 6 miles (9.5 km) inland brings you to the town of Battle, where King Harold’s Saxon army was defeated by William’s Norman invaders. You can visit the former battlefield and ruined abbey, built by William's son on the spot where Harold perished, and explore a medieval gatehouse. Centuries on, walking the trail around the battlefield where thousands died remains a sombre and moving experience. A good pint: Hastings has no shortage of charming local boozers. The 16th-century Stag Inn on All Saints Street has a pretty, tiered garden overlooking the rooftops. Look out for the mummified cat that was found encased within the chimney — a practice said to ward off evil in British folklore. Another good pub is the FILO (First In Last Out) on the High Street, with an unusual indoor fire pit and cosy wooden booths that are always packed on weekends. It brews its own traditional ales and has been joined in recent years by other craft beer makers, including The Brewing Brothers , who run three excellent venues. In the Old Town, the Jenny Lind , named after a 19th-century Swedish opera singer, is one of Hastings' most-loved pubs with regular acoustic nights and folk, rock and sea shanty sessions. Over in St Leonards, The Piper draws a younger crowd and holds regular gigs upstairs. Get festive: Dig out green clothes and flower crowns for the annual "Jack in the Green" folk festival on the first Monday of May. Dancers and drummers dressed in green parade through the town and up on to the West Hill, where the Jack — a crowned figure clad in foliage — is symbolically slain to release the spirit of summer. It's all rather reminiscent of the 1973 folk horror film "The Wicker Man," and seems to get bigger every year. A participant attends the annual May Day bank holiday Jack In The Green parade and festival. REUTERS/Toby Melville Participants attend the annual May Day bank holiday Jack In The Green parade and festival. REUTERS/Toby Melville A participant attends the annual May Day bank holiday Jack In The Green parade and festival. REUTERS/Toby Melville In July, locals rustle up striped shirts and eye patches for Pirate Weekend , which brings three days of live music to the shore, and a noisy parade through the town for all “pirates” to join. In October, an annual bonfire marks the anniversary of the Norman Conquest, with a flaming torch procession through the Old Town and a huge blaze and fireworks on the beach. CITY MEMO DATA POINTS Population: 91,000 Price of a cup of coffee: £3.80 ($5) for a flat white at Starsky & Hatch Price of an ice cream: £3.00 ($4) for a Flake 99 — vanilla soft-serve served in a wafer cone with a small chocolate bar on top — from Dom's Ices . For £3.90 ($5.17), you can get a scoop of gelato at Di Pola's . Great place to see a sunset: The coastal paths of the Country Park, or the West or East Hill

item.title: Record-breaking Renshaw puts Australia on top in Durban
item.description: Matt Renshaw struck a career-best 190 to guide Australia to 390 all out on day two of the first test against South Africa at Kingsmead on Saturday, as the home side reached 27 for one in reply before play was ended prematurely by bad light.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gleeson
item.content:encoded: Matt Renshaw struck a career-best 190 to guide Australia to 390 all out on day two of the first test against South Africa at Kingsmead on Saturday, as the home side reached 27 for one in reply before play was ended prematurely by bad light. Aiden Markram (15 not out) and David Bedingham (12 not out) will resume on the third morning for South Africa, who were frustrated by the record-breaking innings of Renshaw. Ryan Rickelton was the hosts' wicket to fall when he was caught at third slip by Beau Webster for a duck off the bowling of Josh Hazlewood. The day belonged to Renshaw as he shared a record ninth-wicket stand of 134 for Australia against South Africa with Nathan Lyon (27), also the highest partnership for that wicket in Durban. "There was a lot of thinking today while batting," Renshaw said. "How many balls can I face? How do I get off strike when I need to? It was thinking what we can try and do, trying to find the right options, find a boundary if we could. "Keeping them out in the field, getting their quicks coming back on. I saw (Marco) Jansen bowled 30-odd (overs), (Anrich) Nortje 30-odd, so they've got some overs into the frontline bowlers in the first innings of the first game." His score is the highest by a number five batter in tests at Kingsmead, but he was out soon after tea when he edged spinner Simon Harmer to Markram at slip. Australia were in trouble early in Renshaw's innings as they slipped to 124 for six on day one. EARLY TROUBLE But Renshaw flipped the script after putting on 86 for the seventh wicket with skipper Pat Cummins (43). Australia started the second day on 187 for six and frustrated the home side before Wiaan Mulder (4-68) had Cummins caught by Markram at second slip. Mitchell Starc (6) followed quickly after being bowled by Mulder, and at it looked as though South Africa would run through the lower order. Lyon was circumspect, however, and Renshaw rotated the strike superbly to make sure he had most of the strike and continued to accumulate runs rather than attack the bowling. Lyon fell LBW to Marco Jansen (3-68). Renshaw’s 190 has come off 397 balls, a classic test innings of patience and waiting for the bad ball. He was struck in the helmet by speedster Anrich Nortje, but he soon settled again and his second test century came nine years after his first, 185 against Pakistan in 2017. Renshaw had made single-figure scores in 11 of his previous 13 test innings. "He played beautifully throughout the innings, played what was in front of him and left well," Mulder said. "The partnerships built around him and he played the situation as well as anyone could have at this level. "It is a good cricket wicket and will get a bit up and down as the game goes on and spin more."

item.title: Rosatom and Finland's Fennovoima claim different wins after tribunal ruling
item.description: Russia's state nuclear corporation Rosatom and Finnish utility Fennovoima each highlighted different parts of an International Chamber of Commerce (ICC) tribunal ruling as favourable on Saturday, in a long-running dispute over the cancelled Hanhikivi-1 nuclear power project.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russia's state nuclear corporation Rosatom and Finnish utility Fennovoima each highlighted different parts of an International Chamber of Commerce (ICC) tribunal ruling as favourable on Saturday, in a long-running dispute over the cancelled Hanhikivi-1 nuclear power project. The parties have been locked in legal disputes since Fennovoima scrapped the 7-billion-euro ($7.8 billion) project in May 2022, citing significant delays and political risks shortly after Russia launched its conflict in Ukraine . Rosatom said the tribunal found that Fennovoima had unlawfully terminated the contract for the construction of the planned plant in northern Finland. "Today's victory is important, but not final. We will continue to prove that we are right regarding the Finnish project in courts of various instances," Rosatom Director General Alexey Likhachev said in a statement, which did not refer to any financial outcome. Fennovoima said the tribunal found that it had not been entitled to terminate the contract, but that it was entitled to receive reimbursements of advance payments and interest in excess of 1 billion euros ($1.12 billion). It said the tribunal offset both sides' claims, resulting in Rosatom subsidiaries being ordered to pay Fennovoima a net 606 million euros plus interest. The ICC did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The contract to build the 1.2 gigawatt plant was signed in 2013 with Fennovoima, a consortium in which Finnish stakeholders including Fortum, Outokumpu and SSAB originally controlled two thirds through a joint venture, and the Russian side held one third. After the project's termination, Fennovoima wound down its operations and is primarily engaged in legal proceedings. ($1 = 0.8928 euros)

item.title: ゴキブリ党創設者ら拘束、選管トップ抗議封じ込め インド首都厳戒
item.description:
Saurabh Sharma Aftab Ahmed Sakshi Dayal
[ニューデリー １０日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Saurabh Sharma　Aftab Ahmed　Sakshi Dayal

[ニューデリー １０日 ロイター] - インドの警察は１０日、若者中心の団体「ゴキブリ人民党（ＣＪＰ）」の創設者、アビジート・ディプケ氏を拘束した。首都ニューデリーで予定されていた抗議集会を阻止し、参加者や野党の幹部らも拘束した。警察官や準軍事組織の要員数千人が投入され、首都は厳戒態勢にある。

ニューデリーでは、有権者名簿の見直しに関して不正があったとして選挙管理委員会委員長の辞任を求める抗議集会が予定されていた。当局は、抗議集会が始まる前に一帯を封鎖した。

ディプケ氏は抗議集会に参加するため、ムンバイからデリーに到着した航空機内で警察に拘束された。ＣＪＰは指導者らに対する「権威主義的な拘束」を非難。１０日の集会を率いる指導部を機能不全に陥れるための「事前に計画された足止め」だとして、即時釈放を求めた。

テレビ各局の映像によると、野党議員数人、西ベンガル州首相を務めたママタ・バナジー氏やデリー首都圏首相を務めたアルビンド・ケジリワル氏も拘束された。

デジタルニュースメディア２社の代表者によると、デモを取材していた両社の記者計４人が警察に一時拘束された。ロイターの記者１人も拘束されたが、その後、解放された。

最高裁判所の弁護士会会長は、最高裁前で抗議していた弁護士数人が連行されたが、その後解放されたと述べた。

一連の拘束について、警察からのコメントは得られていない。

治安部隊が主要道路や市内への入り口に検問所を設置しした。主要道路には催涙ガス銃を搭載した暴動鎮圧車両が配備され、警官が車両を検査している。ビジネス街ではインターネット接続が遮断され、数十の地下鉄駅や市場が閉鎖されたが、小規模なデモが行われたもようだ。

item.title: Russian attack on Ukrainian city kills 20, a day after Trump eases diesel sanctions on Moscow
item.description: The strike on Zaporizhzhia, which killed three children, came a day after President Trump announced a deal to lift sanctions on Russian diesel.
item.dc:creator: Sergiy Chalyi, Max Hunder
item.content:encoded: Twenty people, including three children, were killed in a Russian attack on the southern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia on Saturday, a day after US President Donald Trump announced a deal to lift sanctions on Russian diesel in a major setback for Kyiv. "Today, Russia said thank you for the lifting of sanctions on diesel exports by dropping five glide bombs on residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia," Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said, in some of his sharpest criticism yet of the White House. Zaporizhzhia has been a regular target of Russian bombardment with strikes [USN:L8N43Z01W TEXT:"intensifying in the past few months."] A 6-year-old girl was among those killed when one strike reduced part of an apartment block to rubble. Her grandfather, Anatoliy Chumniy, stood sobbing over her body, laid on the ground in a white bag, after rescuers pulled it from the wreckage. "Her birthday would have been at the end of the month," he said through tears. Eighteen others were wounded in the attack on the industrial city, with a pre-war population of over 700,000 and whose outskirts lie less than 30 km (20 miles) from the front line. RUSSIA ESCALATING ATTACKS ON UKRAINIAN CITIES It was the third mass-casualty attack on Ukraine this week. Nearly 80 civilians were killed in Russian strikes on Wednesday and Thursday, including at least 30 killed by a bomb in the eastern garrison city of Kramatorsk and 22 others by a missile in the town of Pryluky, 80 miles east of Kyiv. A senior official in Zaporizhzhia, Mykhailo Semikin, said Russia had hit several locations simultaneously in the early hours of Saturday. Rescuers clambered through crumbled masonry to pull other residents of the building out alive. One man, whose leg was trapped in the rubble, screamed in pain as he was being freed. "If (the Russians) have money, they’ll be able to carry on fighting us," said Nataliia Malysheva, a 49-year-old local resident whose parents died in hospital after being pulled from the rubble. "How many lives have been lost here, how many homes have been destroyed? How many innocent people have died in the meantime?" MOSCOW NEEDS 'DIFFERENT SIGNALS' "Last night provided yet more confirmation that Russia perceives any easing of pressure as a signal that it can supposedly keep fighting, that it can supposedly keep dropping bombs on cities. Different signals are needed," Zelenskiy said. A missile attack on Saturday afternoon also hit a restaurant, wounding seven people in Kyiv. Russian drones flew over Kyiv throughout the day, part of a vast new wave of bombardment of the capital, the heaviest since the early days of the war. Russia’s Defence Ministry said on Saturday its drones had struck a data-processing centre in Kyiv and a cargo ship carrying military supplies to the Ukrainian port of Odesa. TRUMP LIFTS DIESEL SANCTIONS Trump's decision to lift sanctions on Russian diesel exports comes as his administration seeks to curb fuel prices, which have risen sharply during the US conflict with Iran . Kyiv had instead urged Washington to increase pressure on Moscow in an effort to force it into serious negotiations to end the four-and-a-half-year war . Trump, meanwhile, has criticised Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries, which he claims have driven up global prices. Kyiv has said it wants a total halt on all energy strikes by both sides as Moscow pummels Ukraine's power grid. On Saturday, parts of Kyiv and the surrounding region were left without power, bringing the city's metro trains to a complete halt for the second time this week. The latest strikes came after Ukrainian and European officials held talks with US negotiators in Miami on Friday aimed at developing a common proposal for ending the war, according to [USN:FWN45V1JO TEXT:"a person familiar with the discussions"]. Trump announced the diesel deal while the negotiations were underway, a move Zelenskiy said had caught Kyiv by surprise. The Ukrainian delegation was headed home on Saturday, presidential aide Dmytro Lytvyn was cited by the Interfax Ukraine news agency as saying. Russian President Vladimir Putin said after a call with Trump that an immediate resumption of peace talks was unlikely, citing Ukrainian drone attacks on Moscow. US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner may visit Moscow within the next two weeks, Russian state news agency TASS reported on Saturday, citing a source. Four civilians were killed and five others were wounded as a result of Ukrainian attacks on the [USN:S8N42201C TEXT:"Russian-controlled Luhansk region"] in eastern Ukraine, the Russian-installed governor said on Saturday. Reuters could not independently verify the report and there was no immediate comment from Ukraine.

item.title: インド、ルピー防衛へドル需要抑制 為替ヘッジ規制を強化
item.description:
Jaspreet Kalra Nimesh Vora
[ムンバイ １０日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Jaspreet Kalra　Nimesh Vora

[ムンバイ １０日 ロイター] - インド準備銀行（中央銀行）は１０日、ルピーが過去最安値近辺で推移する中、相場下支えに向け新たな措置を発表した。石油会社のドル調達を直物市場以外に振り向けるとともに、為替ヘッジ規制を強化する。

ルピーは原油価格や世界的な債券利回りの急上昇を背景に下落圧力が続いており、年初来の下落率は７％を超えている。

中銀は国営石油販売会社３社の日々のドル需要を満たす特別窓口を設け、直物市場への圧力を和らげる。

この仕組みでは、中銀が外貨準備から石油会社に直接ドルを供給する。インディアン・オイル、ヒンドゥスタン・ペトロリアム、バーラト・ペトロリアムの３社が１２日から利用可能となる。

ムンバイを拠点とするＡＮＺ銀行の為替ストラテジスト、ディラジ・ニム氏は「石油会社のドル需要に対応することで、為替市場から最大級の需要源の一つが取り除かれ相場変動の抑制につながるだろう。ただ、外貨準備の減少という形で表れることになる」と述べた。

措置の発表後、薄取引の中ルピーはノンデリバラブル・フォワード（ＮＤＦ）市場で対ドルで約０．６％上昇した。

item.title: モンテネグロがロシア軍事ブロガーを国外退去処分 安保上の理由
item.description: [ベオグラード ９日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[ベオグラード ９日 ロイター] - モンテネグロの警察と国家保安機関は９日、ロシアの有力な軍事ブログ「ルイバリ」の創設者が同国で逮捕され、他のロシア人３人とともに国家安全保障上の理由で国外追放処分になったと発表した。

地元紙ポビエダが関係筋の話として報じたところによると、ロシア国防省の元職員でもあるミハイル・ズビンチュク氏が、妻を含む他のメンバーとともにアドリア海沿岸の保養地リサンで「ロシアの影響力」を広めた容疑で拘束された。

ルイバリはロシアのウクライナでの戦争を扱うブログの中でも特に人気が高く、１５０万人を超える登録者を持つ。投稿したメッセージで、ズビンチュク氏らは合法的にモンテネグロに滞在し、同国の修道院で撮影する予定だったと説明した。

首都ポドゴリツァのロシア大使館は、逮捕の理由について説明を求めたと明らかにした。

ルイバリはロシアの幅広い活動を扱うウェブサイトや情報配信網の一部を構成している。

英国は７月、ルイバリに関係する１０人に制裁を科した。ルイバリはロシア政府から支援を受け、「ウクライナに関する虚偽の言説の拡散や、モルドバ、アルメニアを含む欧州の選挙に干渉してきた責任がある」と非難した。

ロシア政府は、偽情報の拡散や破壊工作展開の疑いを繰り返し否定し、西側が反ロシアのプロパガンダを広めていると主張している。

モンテネグロとロシアの関係は長年、緊張をはらんできた。２０１６年には、モンテネグロ当局がロシアはセルビアの超国家主義者の集団と共謀してクーデターを企てたと非難。ロシア大統領府はこれを否定した。

モンテネグロが１７年に北大西洋条約機構（ＮＡＴＯ）に加盟すると、関係はさらに悪化した。

モンテネグロのスパイッチ首相は今回の逮捕を巡り、同国を不安定化させる試みや、直接的な軍事衝突に至らない行為を指す「ハイブリッド戦」に直面するとの警告があったと述べた。

item.title: 中国、1─9月の都市部新規雇用1052万人 サービス業支援へ
item.description: [北京 １０日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[北京 １０日 ロイター] - 中国人力資源・社会保障省は１０日、１─９月の都市部の新規雇用者数が１０５２万人となり、年間目標の８７．７％を達成したと発表した。同省は、サービス業の雇用拡大に向けた新たな措置を計画している。

同省当局者は記者会見で、１─８月の都市部の調査失業率は平均５．２％で、雇用は「おおむね安定」していたと説明した。

李忠次官兼報道官は、他部門と連携しサービス業の発展を通じて雇用を促進する政策文書を策定する方針を示し、サービス業が雇用吸収の主要な受け皿としての機能を一段と発揮できるようにすると述べた。

李氏はまた、労働集約型産業で雇用を安定的に維持するとともに、新興産業や将来有望な産業で新たな雇用機会を模索していくと表明した。

item.title: Jocelyn Bioh on why Broadway is finally ready for 'School Girls'
item.description: The playwright and actor talks beauty, colorism, and how Broadway has changed in the decade since she wrote the play.
item.dc:creator: Kathryn Lurie
item.content:encoded:
Playwright Jocelyn Bioh during an interview with Reuters in New York City. REUTERS/Brendan McDermid Nearly a decade after Jocelyn Bioh wrote “School Girls; Or, The African Mean Girls Play,” the play itself has barely changed. But the world around it has. The comedy about a group of teenage girls at a Ghanaian boarding school premiered off-Broadway in 2017, launching Bioh’s career as a playwright and going on to become a hit at regional theaters across the United States. But despite its success, Bioh was told it might not belong on Broadway. Now “School Girls” has made it there — following the Broadway success of Bioh’s “Jaja’s African Hair Braiding” in 2023 — and she is finding an audience that responds differently to the play’s exploration of body image, the privileging of lighter skin, known as colorism, and the often brutal social dynamics of girlhood. Beneath its rapid-fire jokes and teenage rivalries is a more painful story about who gets to be considered beautiful — and what people are willing to do to fit that ideal. Speaking in New York City, Bioh discusses what has changed since “School Girls” was first produced, the universality of teenage insecurity and why bringing the play to Broadway feels like coming full circle. This conversation has been edited and condensed for clarity.

How does it feel to finally bring “School Girls” to Broadway? It feels incredibly humbling. This play changed my life. It was the first play of mine that ever got produced. I can very clearly mark what my life was like before opening night of that show and then after. That audiences and critics all still feel the same way nearly a decade later is a reminder that I was on the right track. It also feels doubly exciting because even though it had so much success regionally and has been all over the country, I was told, “It's a great play, but maybe it's not the right fit for a Broadway stage.”

What do you think was meant by that, and what has changed enough for it to be on Broadway now? Broadway shows were very specific then. They didn't have ensembles that looked like the cast of “School Girls.” It was a lot of celebrities, a lot of things that seemed to fit into one specific category or box. The world has shifted. Audiences are different than they were 10 years ago. In a lot of ways, “Jaja's African Hair Braiding” having so much success was a marker that, a Broadway play is just a play that's on Broadway. It doesn't necessarily have to fit a specific category.

Is there anything in the play that hits differently than it did when you first wrote it? The conversation around beauty standards and body image has shifted in the last 10 years. Some would say (for the) better, some would say worse, but we're all aware of it in a different way. The play kicks off with Paulina bullying Nana about her size and her eating. You can feel the audience is immediately on Nana's side. Halfway through the play, she has a moment where she really stands up to Paulina, and every night that moment gets applause. You can feel the audience cheering, almost jumping up ready to fight with her. They're taking off their earrings! We did not have that experience off-Broadway. I think we were in a time where we accepted the idea that if you were somebody who was bigger, you should be losing weight; you should be trying to conform. Our ideas of beauty are very different now. Big ships turn slow, but I appreciate that I can feel that in the audience. Did you rewrite much for this production? Very small things, little jokes that I thought would land better. But the play is still largely the same thing I wrote in 2016. If I were sitting down to write this play now, I don't know that I would be as honest or as vulnerable as I was then, particularly in the moments where Paulina is speaking very directly about how colorism has affected her life. I think I would censor myself a little bit now. I never thought the play would get produced, so I was very free and vulnerable in a way.

Playwright Jocelyn Bioh. REUTERS/Brendan McDermid Why? When you're a playwright and your name starts to grow within the community, you start to have an awareness of the responsibility of your words. And I'm okay with having that responsibility because I know I'm doing something really different. I'm really blowing open how people see Black and African people on a theatrical stage. There's an incredible responsibility to that. The play takes place in Ghana, but these girls feel instantly recognizable. Did you know when you were writing it how universal they would be? I understood that there's a real rich universality we have, particularly in school and friendship dynamics. Those things are evergreen and universal. I knew what I was writing was different, (that) the girls and the people I was reflecting were different, but I didn't want to alienate audiences. That's part of why I added the subtitle. What's something we all know and recognize about the teenage experience? Mean girls. Paulina seems to believe that if she can just become Miss Ghana, she can escape the limits of her life. Is her obsession with beauty really an obsession with power and possibility? Probably. Ultimately, I think she really believes this is going to set her up for a successful life in entertainment. The play is set in 1986, and if you became Miss Ghana, Miss World, Miss Universe — any of those things — you could become a star. This is how we have Vanessa Williams or Halle Berry or Kenya Moore, if you're of the “Real Housewives” persuasion. (Another character,) Eloise, is a former Miss Ghana and did leave. She's come back now living a different life, (signifying that) in order to have success, you've got to get out. In order to have power, you have to get out. Maybe Paulina doesn't see the beauty and power that she can build in her own country. That's reflective of so many immigrant, particularly African immigrant, stories: In order to have success, you need to leave. I don't know if the play were set in 2026, (if) that would be the case now. I think the play would be very different. But for Paulina and her circumstances then, that is what she believed. The play deals so directly with colorism. Do you think colorism is in some ways more sensitive to talk about than racism? They're inextricably linked. The play largely talks about and shows the effects of colorism, but then ends with a global lesson on racism. And we've not moved on from it. When we started rehearsals for the play in August, the biggest news story was Lupita Nyong'o playing Helen of Troy in Christopher Nolan's film (“The Odyssey”). (Her casting) did not fit with whomever's standard of beauty (for) the woman whose face launched a thousand ships. Why didn't it fit? Why were there so many suggestions about, “Well, Zendaya's in the movie, why can't she play that part?” That's a very clear conversation about colorism, whether people are using that word or not.

When I wrote this play, it was really important for me to have that conversation because it had affected my life so much. Revisiting it now, especially in relation to these conversations that are happening globally, I'm like, well, we've not moved on from it. We can't move on from colorism because nobody's moved on from racism. I can't change people's minds. But if people come to see “School Girls” and their implicit bias can shift just a little bit, then I've done my job. The play is extremely funny until you realize how much pain is sitting underneath the humor. How deliberate is that? I really believe that comedy is just a funny way of being serious. Humor and pain are on two different sides of a truth coin. It's all rooted in truth. Paulina is a girl in the world who's trying to be affirmed and validated that she belongs there, that her beauty is widely accepted even if she knows that it's not. The lengths she goes to get there are what's comical, but it's rooted in something real that we all experience. At the end of the day, I'm a comedic writer and I want people to be entertained. But because I know the responsibility of who I'm introducing and the culture I'm introducing, I think there's a responsibility in also educating people. If I can make that medicine go down with a little bit of sugar, honey, agave, whatever you like, I'm willing to go there. The perspectives expressed in Culture Current are the subject’s own and do not necessarily reflect the views of Reuters News.

item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Yimou Lee　Ben Blanchard

[台北 １０日 ロイター] - 台湾の頼清徳総統は１０日、双十節（建国記念日）の演説で、台湾は平和を大切にするが自由を放棄することはないと述べ、台湾の人々が生存する権利は尊重されなければならないと訴えた。防衛力の強化は挑発ではないとも強調した。

台湾は中国から軍事的・政治的圧力の強化に直面している。中国は一貫して台湾を自国領土と主張しているが、台湾は強く反対している。

台湾は防衛費を増額し軍の近代化を進めているが、 対峙する中国軍の規模ははるかに大きく、ステルス戦闘機や空母、多数のミサイルなどの先進的兵器の配備を進めている。

頼氏は総統府前で演説し、平和は「願い」だけでは実現できないと強調。

「台湾は平和を大切にするが、自由を放棄しない。交流には前向きだが、従属は受け入れない」と語った。

また、「権威主義の拡張」に直面する中で、台湾の決意は自らの存続だけに関わるものではないと指摘。

「力がルールに優越することはなく、強者が人々から自らの未来を決める権利を奪うことはできないと、国際社会が今も信じているかどうかの問題だ」と続けた。

防衛投資の拡大については、戦争を挑発するためではなく抑止するためだとして、「対話を放棄するためではなく、対等と尊厳を基礎として対話が行われるようにするために自衛力を強化している」と語った。

頼氏が総統として初めて双十節演説を行った２０２４年の直後、中国は台湾周辺で軍事演習を実施したが、昨年は行わなかった。

台湾周辺で中国が最後に軍事演習を行ったのは昨年１２月下旬で、台湾向けとして過去最大となる１１０億ドル規模の米国の武器売却の報道を受けたものだった。

頼氏は、米国と中国が対話を通じて競争を管理し、紛争や戦争のリスクを低減していることを歓迎すると述べた。

item.title: 米、台湾沖の中国の活動を非難 「著しく安定を損なう」
item.description:
[台北 １０日 ロイター] - 米国務省は、台湾東岸沖での中国の海洋活動は「安定を著しく損なう」もので、緊張を悪化させるだけだとの認識を示した。ロイターは先に、８月に同海域で中国の海上民兵船が初めて確認されたと報じていた。
中国は６月以降、沿岸警備隊による定期的な巡視を含め、台湾東岸沖での活動を強化している。
台湾の当局者は、中国が軍、準軍事組織、民間の船舶などを重層的に運用し、海上封鎖の可能性を想定した訓練を行っているとみている。
台湾は、封鎖や有事の際に友好国からの補給ルートとして東岸沖の海域を極めて重要と位置付けている。
米国務省の報道官は、海上民兵の船舶目撃に関する質問に答える形で、米国は台湾東方沖での中国の活動を引き続き懸念していると述べ、「中国の行動は安定を著しく損なうものだ
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[台北 １０日 ロイター] - 米国務省は、台湾東岸沖での中国の海洋活動は「安定を著しく損なう」もので、緊張を悪化させるだけだとの認識を示した。ロイターは先に、８月に同海域で中国の海上民兵船が初めて確認されたと報じていた。

中国は６月以降、沿岸警備隊による定期的な巡視を含め、台湾東岸沖での活動を強化している。

台湾の当局者は、中国が軍、準軍事組織、民間の船舶などを重層的に運用し、海上封鎖の可能性を想定した訓練を行っているとみている。

台湾は、封鎖や有事の際に友好国からの補給ルートとして東岸沖の海域を極めて重要と位置付けている。

米国務省の報道官は、海上民兵の船舶目撃に関する質問に答える形で、米国は台湾東方沖での中国の活動を引き続き懸念していると述べ、「中国の行動は安定を著しく損なうものだ 」と指摘。

その上で「台湾が７０年以上にわたり平穏に管理してきた海域に対する権限を主張することで中国は緊張を悪化させ、自ら目指すとしている問題の平和的解決を損なっているだけだ」と述べた。

また、米国は中国政府に対し、台湾への圧力をやめ「台湾の民主的に選出された当局と意義ある対話」を行うよう求めているとした。

中国外務省はコメント要請に応じていない。

item.title: トランプ氏、平和賞逃し批判 「ノルウェーに消えない汚点」
item.description:
Jacob Bogage
[シラキュース（米ニューヨーク州） ９日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Jacob Bogage

[シラキュース（米ニューヨーク州） ９日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は９日、ノーベル平和賞を受賞できなかったことへの不満を改めて表明し、恥ずべき不名誉な決定でノーベル委員会の本拠地であるノルウェーに汚点を残したと批判した。

委員会は、２０２６年の平和賞を国際刑事裁判所（ＩＣＣ）の元判事ナビ・ピレイ氏に授与すると発表した。同氏は、イスラエルがパレスチナ自治区ガザでジェノサイド（集団虐殺）を行ったと結論付けた国連報告書の取りまとめを主導した。

トランプ氏はニューヨーク州シラキュースでの選挙集会で、ピレイ氏を「正体不明の人物」と呼び「その人物のことは聞いたこともない。誰も知らなかった」と述べた。

トランプ氏は大統領就任以来毎年、平和賞を受賞できなかったことに失望を表明してきた。

トランプ氏は「これはノルウェーという国と、こうした不名誉で恥ずべき決定を下した人々にとって、消すことのできない汚点だ」と述べた。

その上で、自ら解決に関与したと主張する複数の紛争を列挙。根拠は示さなかったが、韓国と北朝鮮、日本と北朝鮮、中国と台湾の間での戦争勃発の回避に貢献したと主張した。

「ノーベル平和賞の信用は、反民主主義的で、まさに文明の敵である一握りの過激な思想の持ち主によって永遠に失われた。ノルウェーよ、われわれは忘れない」と述べた。

item.title: サッカー＝マンＣのマレスカ監督がクラブ擁護、「タイトルの価値に傷なし」
item.description: ［マンチェスター（英国） ９日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［マンチェスター（英国）　９日　ロイター］ - サッカーのイングランド・プレミアリーグ、マンチェスター・シティー（マンＣ）のエンツォ・マレスカ監督は９日、財務規定違反の問題を抱えている同クラブを擁護した。

マンＣは１１日に行われるプレミアリーグで、先月末に１００件以上の重大な財務規定違反を認定されて以降初の試合となる敵地でのリバプール戦を迎える。クラブはすべての不正行為を否定しており、１日に不服申し立てを行った。

ジョゼップ・グアルディオラ監督の下で３冠を達成した２０２２─２３シーズンにコーチ陣の一員だったマレスカ監督は、リバプール戦に向けた記者会見で、「当時、選手やクラブ、ペップ（グアルディオラ監督）がどれほど努力したか私はよく知っている。だから、その功績を疑う余地など全くない」と語った。また、功績に汚点があると感じるかと問われると、「全くない」と答えた。

６月にグアルディオラ監督の後任として指揮官に就任したマレスカ監督は、契約交渉中に財務規定違反の疑惑に関する話題が上がったことは一度もなかったと明かし、「私はクラブを信頼している。だからこそ、このクラブに加わった。ここ以外に自分がいたいと思うクラブもない。ここにいられることをとても嬉しく思っているし、就任した初日からずっと誇りに感じている」とコメント。就任前に今回の問題の展開を知っていたとしても、「間違いなく」監督職を引き受けていただろうと語った。

item.title: Isaias kills four, about 670,000 without power after landfall
item.description: The National Hurricane Center expects storm surges, flash flooding, damaging winds and a risk of tornadoes across parts of the US Southeast.
item.dc:creator: Rhea Abraham, Rajveer Pardesi, Marianna Parraga
item.content:encoded: Four people died after Hurricane Isaias made landfall early on Saturday, and about 670,000 residents in Florida, Alabama, Georgia and Mississippi were still without power as the storm weakened to a post-tropical cyclone, according to local authorities and electricity monitoring services. Two of the deaths resulted from trees falling on homes, according to local media and authorities. Authorities in Florida had received no search and rescue requests shortly after landfall in a sign of limited impact, Governor Ron DeSantis said. But hazardous conditions remained and storm surges, flash flooding, damaging winds and a risk of tornadoes across parts of the US Southeast were expected, the National Hurricane Center said. The tornado threat is expected to continue on Saturday across parts of the Florida Panhandle, Georgia and the Carolinas, the NHC said. In Florida, power restoration was marked as a priority, authorities said, while highways, bridges and airports were reopening, and teams were assessing the damage. "They're going to make assessments this morning, and I think that'll give us a good sense about the future for the rapidity of the power restoration," DeSantis told a press conference in Tallahassee. Some 16,000 utility linemen had prepared to respond to the storm, he said. About 420,000 customers in Florida, 190,000 in Alabama, 43,000 in Georgia and 17,000 in Mississippi had no power as of midday Saturday, according to tracking firm PowerOutage.us. A separate storm on the Pacific Ocean, Rachel, was moving toward the coast of northern Baja California on Saturday, bringing wind gusts and increased tides, which left another 7,000 people without power in California. Alabama's emergency management agency said the downed trees and power lines made travel hazardous in Houston County, which is under a flash flood warning. "Due to the impacts of Hurricane Isaias, all Houston County roads are closed until further notice," it posted on X. A category 2 hurricane when it hit Florida's coast and the first of the 2026 Atlantic season, Isaias is expected to produce gusty winds well inland before weakening below gale force later on Saturday, the NHC said. On Saturday, oil and gas producer Shell (SHEL.L) said it was beginning to redeploy personnel to its Mars, Olympus, Ursa, Vito and Appomattox assets in the Gulf, while Chevron (CVX.N) was advancing efforts to redeploy staff to its platforms and seeking to restore full production. "Remobilization of crews will continue through Sunday," it said. Despite the progress, about 69% of oil output and 57% of natural gas production in the US Gulf of Mexico remained shut on Saturday, slightly down from Friday numbers, the Marine Minerals Administration said. Some 113 production platforms representing 30% of the total remained evacuated, according to the agency. President Donald Trump, asked about hurricane preparations on Friday, told reporters outside the White House that it was "under control." The US Energy Department said on Saturday it authorized an emergency exchange of up to 4 million barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to address supply disruptions due to the hurricane. Emergency declarations were approved in Florida and Alabama to ensure federal resources would be available to respond to Isaias, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said on X. "There's also a lot of hazards post-storm that people should be careful of, but so far, we've had a lot of assets in place that have not been called on," DeSantis told FOX News early on Saturday. In the coastal city of Pensacola, a lack of drinking water is a problem, the mayor said. Pensacola airport, Florida's 10th largest, was damaged by the storm and is closed to commercial flights until further notice.

item.title: サッカー＝監視対象の選手・関係者の過半数が誹謗中傷受信、ＦＩＦＡ発表
item.description: ［９日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［９日　ロイター］ - 国際サッカー連盟（ＦＩＦＡ）は９日、２０２６年ワールドカップ（Ｗ杯）北中米３カ国大会においてソーシャルメディア保護サービス（ＳＭＰＳ）によって監視された選手、監督、関係者の計１６０６人のうち、半数以上がオンライン上で誹謗中傷を受けていたと発表した。

監視対象となった１６０６人のうち８１２人が、誹謗中傷と分類されるメッセージを少なくとも１件受信した。差別的な誹謗中傷の中で最も多かったのは人種差別に関するもので、誹謗中傷全体の１２％を占めた。一般的な誹謗中傷を除くと、その割合は２０％に上った。

最も標的とされた特定の個人は１万件以上の誹謗中傷投稿を受け取り、そのうち４０％が人種差別的な内容だった。

ＳＭＰＳは１７１０万件の投稿やコメントを分析し、そのうち約２４万件が人の目による精査を経て誹謗中傷であると確認された。２９０５のアカウントについて調査が必要と判断され、７８６アカウントが審査のため法執行機関に報告された。

投稿監視ツールは、ＦＩＦＡおよび加盟協会の公式チャンネルにおける６０７０万件のコメントをスキャンし、スパムを含め９２０万件を非表示にした。

item.title: ＭＬＢ＝ドジャース山本、リーグ優勝決定Ｓ第2戦で先発へ 初戦はスクバル
item.description: ［９日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［９日　ロイター］ - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）ドジャースのデーブ・ロバーツ監督は９日、ブルワーズとのナ・リーグ優勝決定シリーズ（７回戦制）で、１１日の第１戦にタリク・スクバル投手、１２日の第２戦に山本由伸投手を先発させると明らかにした。ＭＬＢ公式サイトが伝えた。

ドジャースはブレーブスとの地区シリーズを３勝１敗で突破。先発したスクバル、ブレーク・スネル、山本、タイラー・グラスノーの４投手は計２１回１／３を投げて自責４、防御率１．６９を記録した。今季のプレーオフ出場チームではレイズの先発陣に次ぐ２番目の好成績となっている。

地区シリーズで第３戦に先発した山本は７回を４安打１失点、１四球、１０三振と好投。中５日で第２戦に登板する予定で、シリーズが第６戦までもつれた場合も通常の登板間隔で先発できる見込み。

山本は昨年のワールドシリーズで最優秀選手（ＭＶＰ）に選出され、最終第７戦では前日の登板から休養なしで救援登板した。今季のプレーオフでも短い登板間隔や救援での起用に応じる意向を示しているが、球団は可能な限り通常の登板間隔を維持する方針。

スネルがリーグ優勝決定シリーズ第３戦、グラスノーが第４戦に先発する可能性がある。ドジャースは昨年まで２年連続でワールドシリーズを制しており、３連覇を目指す。

item.title: Ｆ１＝シンガポールＧＰスプリント予選、フェルスタッペンがトップ
item.description: ［シンガポール ９日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［シンガポール　９日　ロイター］ - 自動車レースＦ１の第１７戦、シンガポール・グランプリ（ＧＰ）は９日、スプリント予選を行い、レッドブルのマックス・フェルスタッペン（オランダ）がトップタイムを記録した。

フェルスタッペンは１分３１秒１５６をマークし、２番手のジョージ・ラッセル（英国、メルセデス）に０秒１２０差をつけた。シンガポールでは過去に、ポールポジション（ＰＰ）獲得も優勝もともに経験していなかった。

フェルスタッペンは「ソフトタイヤを装着すると、マシンが少し生き返ったように感じた。トップになれるとは予想していなかったので、とてもうれしい」とコメントした。

３番手はシャルル・ルクレール（モナコ、フェラーリ）。総合首位のキミ・アントネッリ（イタリア、メルセデス）は７番手だった。

ラッセルは同日のフリー走行でトップタイムを記録したが、パワーユニットの部品交換に伴い、１１日の決勝では計４０グリッド降格のペナルティーを受ける。ただ、１０日のスプリントには影響しない。

スプリント予選の最初のセッションでは、セルヒオ・ペレス（メキシコ、キャデラック）が防護壁に衝突し、コース上に破片が散乱したため赤旗中断となった。その後、計時システムの不具合で第２セッションの開始が遅れたほか、追い抜き支援機能の作動にも問題が発生した。

item.title: India detains thousands, locks down Delhi to foil election chief protest
item.description: Thousands of police and paramilitary personnel deployed across the city, mobile internet services were suspended and dozens of metro stations and markets were shut as authorities moved to stop a rally organized by the Cockroach movement.
item.dc:creator: Saurabh Sharma, Sarita Singh, Sakshi Dayal
item.content:encoded: Police detained more than 2,000 protesters and the founder of the "Cockroach" youth movement in Delhi on Saturday as security forces [USN:L1N45V075 TEXT:"locked down"] parts of the capital to thwart a rally demanding the resignation of India's election chief. Thousands of police and paramilitary personnel were deployed across the city, mobile internet services were suspended in the central business district and dozens of metro stations and markets were shut as authorities moved to stop a demonstration organised by the Cockroach movement. The protest was aimed at Chief Election Commissioner [USN:L4N45K0DB TEXT:"Gyanesh Kumar"] over a [USN:L1N45V037 TEXT:"revision of voter lists"] that critics say disproportionately benefits Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The movement had planned to gather thousands of people at Jantar Mantar in central Delhi, but the area was sealed off by security forces before the demonstration began. A home ministry official, speaking on condition of anonymity, told Reuters more than 2,000 people were detained in Delhi. Local media said about 400 protesters were held in India's financial hub, Mumbai. There was no immediate comment from police on the detentions. The United Nations human rights office expressed concerns over mass detentions before and during the protests. "We call on the authorities to ensure that the right to peaceful assembly is fully respected and fulfilled," UN Human Rights Spokesperson Thameen Al-Kheetan said in a statement. He also urged authorities to engage in "meaningful dialogue" to address the "broadly held" concerns expressed. The Indian mission to the UN in Geneva, however, called the UN's concerns "misplaced" and said they constitute "an unwarranted interference in the internal affairs of India." It stressed that the right to peaceful assembly was guaranteed by India's Constitution. "As in every democracy, Indian citizens exercise this right subject to reasonable restrictions in the interest of public order," the statement added. MOVEMENT LEADERS HELD Police detained Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke and senior leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka when their flight from Mumbai landed in Delhi, the group said in a statement. Television footage showed Dipke challenging officers who approached him on board the aircraft. "I have come to be arrested, arrest me ... I am not afraid of you guys," he said. "No, this is not an arrest," one officer replied. "Please cooperate." The movement condemned what it called the "authoritarian detention" of its leaders, demanded their release and vowed to continue protesting. "We will continue our protest tomorrow, day after ... until Gyanesh Kumar resigns. We will be on the streets," CJP leader Ajinkya Shinde told reporters. CJP also said authorities refused to provide updates on the leaders' whereabouts or health, even after news arrived of the death of Dipke's grandmother. Police said Dipke was informed of her death and was offered help to return home for the funeral. Some opposition lawmakers and former chief ministers Mamata Banerjee of West Bengal, Arvind Kejriwal of Delhi, and Pinarayi Vijayan of Kerala were also detained, TV channels showed. Representatives of two digital news outlets said police briefly detained four of their reporters while they were covering the demonstrations. A Reuters journalist was also detained briefly before being released. Across the capital of about 20 million people, security forces set up checkpoints on major roads and entry points, boarded buses searching for protesters and inspected vehicles. Barricades and concrete blocks disrupted traffic while anti-riot vehicles equipped with tear-gas launchers guarded key routes. NEW CHALLENGE TO MODI The demonstrations represent one of the most serious tests yet for Modi, stemming from allegations that election authorities improperly revised voter rolls ahead of recent state polls. Protests intensified after the Indian Express reported last week that two election commissioners had questioned Kumar's voter-list revisions that removed roughly 130 million names from voter lists. Kumar has not commented but the Election Commission and the BJP have denied allegations of wrongdoing. The BJP says its electoral success reflects Modi's popularity and India's economic growth, and accuses opposition parties of spreading misinformation. The near [USN:L6N45U0IF TEXT:"daily protests"] come just months after demonstrations over exam paper leaks forced his [USN:L1N43R02E TEXT:"education minister to quit"]. The unrest also comes ahead of a series of important state elections beginning in early 2027. Rahul Gandhi, leader of the main opposition Congress party, said Modi's opponents would not back down. A senior BJP member, Ravi Shankar Prasad, said the party was not opposed to demonstrations but the street protests had been "weaponised" by rivals due to election defeats. DELETIONS AFFECTED STATE POLLS, OPPOSITION ALLEGES Opposition parties say the deletions affected the outcome of recent state elections won by the BJP and have cast a shadow over voting in the world's largest democracy. Election Commission data show about 130 million voter entries were removed during the verification exercise, including 63 million people who had relocated, 30 million who could not be traced and 28 million who had died. The commission says the removals relate to entries identified during the draft revision process and that any eligible voter incorrectly deleted can re-enrol.

item.title: ＮＢＡ＝レブロン、シクサーズでのプレシーズン初戦で10得点
item.description: ［９日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［９日　ロイター］ - 米プロバスケットボール協会（ＮＢＡ）のセブンティシクサーズに加入したレブロン・ジェームズ（４１）は８日、ネッツとのプレシーズン戦で移籍後初出場を果たし、１０得点５アシストを記録した。

レブロンはフィールドゴールの試投がわずか１本だったものの、フリースロー８本を全て成功させた。プレーしたのは前半のみで後半は出場せず、シクサーズは１０８─１１４で敗れた。

レブロンは試合後、「新しいユニホームを着ていたのは確かだが、バスケットボールはバスケットボール。コート上でプレーするものだ」と語り、これまで練習でともに汗を流してきたチームメートと実戦に臨めたことを喜んだ。

レブロンは７月、フリーエージェント（ＦＡ）として２年総額８００万ドル（約１２億７０００万円）、選手オプション付きの契約で加入。昨季はレーカーズで６０試合に出場し、１試合平均２０．９得点６．１リバウンド７．２アシストを記録した。

オールスター選出２２回を誇るレブロンは、通算出場試合数（１６２２）と通算得点（４万３４４０）でＮＢＡ歴代最多記録を保持。ヒートで２回、キャバリアーズとレーカーズで各１回、ＮＢＡ制覇を果たしている。

item.title: サッカー＝ＰＳＶが白星、佐野航大フル出場
item.description: ［９日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［９日　ロイター］ - サッカーのオランダ１部は９日、１試合を行い、佐野航大が所属するＰＳＶアイントホーフェンはホームでヘーレンフェーンに２─０で勝利した。

佐野が先発したＰＳＶは前半２９分、右サイドからのクロスを相手ＧＫが弾くと、これをフース・ティルが頭で押し込んで先制。後半２３分にはＣＫから相手のオウンゴールを誘発した。佐野はフル出場した。

開幕から６勝１分け１敗としたＰＳＶは、暫定２位につけている。

item.title: ゴルフ＝米沢が20位、松山は30位に後退 ベイカレントクラシック
item.description: ［９日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［９日　ロイター］ - 米男子ゴルフの秋季シリーズ、ベイカレント・クラシック・レクサスは９日、神奈川県横浜ＣＣ（パー７１）で第２ラウンドを行い、米沢蓮が日本勢最高の２０位につけた。

前日１７位の米沢は４バーディー、２ボギーの６９で回り、通算５アンダーの１３７。１２位スタートの松山英樹は３バーディー、４ボギーの７２とスコアを落とし、通算３アンダーの３０位に後退した。

同じく１２位で出た久常涼は７１で回り、通算４アンダーの１３８で２６位。金谷拓実と砂川公佑は３０位、岩田寛と石坂友宏は３８位、藤本佳則と細野勇策は４６位、香妻陣一朗は５４位、中島啓太は６１位、岩崎亜久竜は６３位、アマチュアの長崎煌心は７０位だった。

首位には通算１１アンダーでキース・ミッチェルとジェーコブ・ブリッジマン（ともに米国）が並んだ。ミッチェルは８バーディー、２ボギーの６５で６つ伸ばし、ブリッジマンは４バーディー、１ボギーの６８で回った。

item.title: サッカー＝2位リヨンがランスに屈し初黒星、中村は途中出場
item.description: ［ランス（フランス） ９日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［ランス（フランス）　９日　ロイター］ - サッカーのフランス１部は９日、１試合を行い、２位リヨンは敵地でＲＣランスに１─２で敗れ、今季初黒星を喫した。リヨンの中村敬斗は後半１５分から途中出場した。

リヨンは前後半に１点ずつ奪われて２点のビハインドを背負ったが、後半３９分に相手が退場者を出して数的優位に立つと、直後に１９歳カリス・メラが相手守備陣のミスを突いて１点を返した。しかし、反撃もそこまでで、開幕からの無敗が途絶えた。

リヨンは勝ち点１１で暫定２位。一方、ＲＣランスは同７とし、１５位から暫定７位に浮上した。

item.title: テニス＝マスターズ上海大会、坂本が3回戦進出 ジョコビッチは敗退
item.description: ［上海 ９日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［上海　９日　ロイター］ - テニスのマスターズ上海大会は９日、男子シングルス２回戦を行い、予選勝者の坂本怜が第２３シードでロシア出身のアンドレイ・ルブレフを６─４、６─４のストレートで破り、３回戦進出を果たした。

世界ランキング１３７位の坂本は第１セットの第１ゲームでブレークに成功。第２セットも第９ゲームで相手のサービスゲームを破り、元世界５位の格上選手から金星を挙げた。３回戦では第９シードのアレックス・デミノー（オーストラリア）と対戦する。

過去４回優勝の第１０シード、ノバク・ジョコビッチ（セルビア）はフベルト・フルカチュ（ポーランド）に４─６、３─６で敗れ、初戦で姿を消した。

ジョコビッチはこれまでフルカチュとの対戦で８戦全勝だった。試合後、「北京でプレーしていた時の状態には程遠かった。少し疲れていて、フレッシュではなかった」と振り返った。

第１シードのアレクサンダー・ズベレフ（ドイツ）、第３シードのベン・シェルトン（米国）は順当に勝利した。

item.title: サッカー＝なでしこジャパン、ハイチに5得点で大勝 国際親善試合
item.description: ［９日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［９日　ロイター］ - サッカーの女子日本代表「なでしこジャパン」は９日、パリ近郊のサントゥアンでハイチとの国際親善試合を行い、５─１で大勝した。

前半に清家貴子が先制点を挙げた日本は、浜野まいか、長谷川唯のゴールで加点。１点を返されて３─１とリードして迎えた後半には、途中出場の千葉玲海菜、土方麻椰もネットを揺らした。

日本はこの後、１３日にドイツのブレーメンでドイツと対戦する。

SAN FRANCISCO, Oct 9 : Six-month-old microchip startup Nuvacore, which does not yet have a product, is raising hundreds of millions of dollars at a roughly $2.5 billion valuation to develop a new central processor designed for data centers, according to two people familiar with the fundraising. Nuvacore is seeking to raise the funds as the appetite for central processors has swollen due to the thirst for data-crunching capacity to power chatbots such as Anthropic's Claude. CPUs perform vital functions as traffic controllers for Nvidia's AI chips and run autonomous AI software known as agents.  The roughly $2.5 billion valuation has not been previously reported. The Information reported previously that Nuvacore was raising $200 million or more. The funding round has not closed, and the people cautioned that the valuation and size of the capital raise could change. Intel and Advanced Micro Devices, which use x86 technology, have long dominated the data center CPU market. Companies designing chips based on Arm's technology — found inside Amazon and Microsoft custom CPUs — have also attempted to make inroads in the data center market.

Nuvacore has not yet developed a product. Last month, it described an unconventional design strategy: to build the core functionality of the chip before committing to an architecture such as the x86 used by Intel and AMD, or Arm, which is used in most mobile phones.  The design strategy will allow the company's engineers to avoid the limitations and requirements of specific architectures and optimize a design for the type of computations that are most common in data centers and AI infrastructure, Nuvacore said. Nuvacore declined to comment. The San Jose, California-based startup was founded by renowned engineers Gerard Williams, John Bruno and Ram Srinivasan. Williams, a former Apple executive, sold a prior startup called Nuvia to Qualcomm for $1.4 billion in 2021. Nuvacore earlier this year announced a seed funding round led by Sequoia Capital. It joins a series of young chip startups that have sought billion-dollar valuations before releasing a product as investor appetite for AI hardware companies has returned. Over the past decade, Silicon Valley venture capital firms have taken much less interest in hardware than software because of hardware's longer development cycles, higher capital needs and the industry's cyclical demand. Investors put about $10.7 billion into semiconductor startups in the first five months of 2026, already outpacing the $12.2 billion raised globally in all of 2025, according to Crunchbase data. Earlier this year, Intel said it could not manufacture enough chips to meet demand, and was able to sell products it had previously determined were too faulty for sale. AMD also described swelling CPU sales in a recent results conference call with analysts. Shares in both companies have risen more than 180 per cent this year. Nvidia launched a CPU called Vera this year. CEO Jensen Huang has said the company expects to sell $20 billion worth of its Vera CPU in this fiscal year, which ends in January.

Source: Reuters
